$comment: tools/cpu-sweep.ts reads this. `machines` scales each CPU model to the AMD EPYC 7763 (factor 1): a factor is the median, over routes confirmed in every run, of the route's raw median on the 7763 divided by its raw median on that model, from `runs` runs (2026-10-09). A model with no entry reads raw and --gate judges nothing on it; a model needs two runs before it gets a factor. No laptop is listed: a laptop's other work inflates every reading at once (an M3 Max read 1.7x higher on one run than the run before), so a local run reads raw and gets no verdict. `routes` lets a route stay up to its own ceilingMs, in EPYC 7763 ms, with the reason it costs that much today: the highest of 14 scaled CI runs plus 20%, rounded up to the half millisecond, for every route whose highest reading plus 20% passed the 8 ms gate. --gate fails on an entry for a route the sweep doesn't know, and prints an entry whose route reads under 4 ms as stale, so the list only shrinks. `control.ms` is the /robots.txt control's usual median in EPYC 7763 ms, from the 9 EPYC 7763 runs since #1267 (2026-10-09). A run whose scaled control reads more than `control.drift` off it is inconclusive. 29 ordinary runs on three models read from 8% under to 16% over, and the EPYC 9V74 runner that false-failed #1273 read 33% over. If every run starts to drift the same way, the dispatcher's own cost moved: re-measure `ms` from EPYC 7763 runs.
